# Masthead

> Masthead is the layer between a website and the person who manages it. A website's theme declares what its owner can change; Masthead builds the site's admin from that declaration and runs the site: hosting, custom domains with automatic TLS, content storage and publishing. It is open source.

Masthead reverses the usual CMS relationship. Instead of one generic admin that every website must fit inside, each theme's manifest.json declares site-wide settings, the fields every post and page carries, and page templates with their own fields. Masthead turns that into the management interface for that one website. The builder controls design, structure and the editing experience; the owner gets content and only the settings that matter.

Masthead is free to publish on: unlimited posts and pages, marketplace themes, and a masthead.site subdomain with automatic HTTPS. A paid site license adds a custom domain, collaborators and statistics. The full source is on GitHub, so it can be self-hosted or audited.

Key ideas:

- Theme-defined admin: settings, post and page fields, and page types come from the theme, so owners see only what their website needs.
- Themes are Liquid templates, a stylesheet and a manifest, packaged as a zip and shared through the marketplace.
- Platform around the theme: hosting, custom domains with automatic TLS, media uploads, multiple sites per account, collaboration, cookieless statistics, and generated sitemap.xml, robots.txt, llms.txt and structured data.
- Deliberately not a page builder, a plugin platform or an application framework.

## Pages

- [Home](https://masthead.site/): how Masthead works, examples and FAQ
- [Pricing](https://masthead.site/pricing): free plan and the paid site license
- [Theme marketplace](https://masthead.site/marketplace): browse published themes
- [Verified themes](https://masthead.site/marketplace/verified): themes reviewed by the Masthead team
- [Community themes](https://masthead.site/marketplace/community): themes published by users
